2.text: tent. On the fourth day the cord is untied, and the woman may then stay

3.text: in the outer tent, busying herself about her household duties.

4.text: BLOOD-PAINTING. — On the fifth day, the ceremony of blood-painting is

5.text: performed. For this the woman with the child is put into the family sledge,

6.text: with one reindeer attached, and is carried around the outer tent, following

7.text: the direction of the sun’s course. The sledge is brought to a stop at the

8.text: sacrificing-place behind the tent,¹ where all the charms and images are arranged,
8.note: Footnote marker superscript 1 (U+00B9) after 'tent,'; draft misread it as lowercase l.

9.text: ready for the sacrifice. The reindeer that drew the sledge is slaughtered;

10.text: and the mother with the child, and at least two other members of the family,

11.text: paint on their faces the usual blood-marks. The charms, and also the three

12.text: central poles of the tent-frame, are also painted with blood. The woman

13.text: takes the sinews out of the legs of the reindeer, and stores them away to be

14.text: used as her boot-strings. Neglect to do this brings on pains in the legs,

16.text: The ceremony of blood-painting is in many cases performed sooner, even

17.text: on the second day after delivery. This haste is attributable to the idea that,

18.text: before the ceremony, the new-born child is highly susceptible to evil influence;

19.text: while after that, it is under the protection of family charms and sacred things.

20.text: Before the ceremony is performed, no person coming from outside is

21.text: allowed to enter the house, especially in the evening. Even the father of

22.text: the child, should he come from a visit to the herd, must first enter a neigh-

23.text: bor’s house, or at least rub against his body a small pup, which, as said

24.text: before,² will overcome the evil influence. After the ceremony, these precautions
24.note: Footnote marker superscript 2 (U+00B2) after 'before,'; draft misread it as '?'.

25.text: are not in force, and are renewed only when contagious diseases are prevalent,

26.text: or when the child is suffering. In this latter case it is also forbidden to sell,

27.text: or give away to strangers, anything belonging to the house, as the child’s

28.text: health might be given away with the object.

29.text: It so happened that several times, on my arrival at a Chukchee camp,

30.text: I was refused admission to the houses, in order to protect the children from

31.text: evil influences; and some of these experiences were not extremely happy.
